newsitem.title: USA: Travelers Group profits jump 23 percent, hit record.
newsitem.headline: Travelers Group profits jump 23 percent, hit record.

text.p: Travelers Group, the giant insurance and financial services company, said Monday its profits raced ahead by 23 percent in the third quarter, reaching a record $1.7 billion for the year to date.

Travelers said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 climbed to $591.8 million, or $1.18 a share, from $481.4 million, or 96 cents a share. Revenues for the quarter increased 25 percent to $5.6 billion from $4.5 billion.

The company said its earnings included net investment portfolio losses of $15.0 million, as well as a $30.7 million after-tax gain related to a contingency payment from its 1995 sale of The MetraHealth Companies.
Travelers said its operating earnings for the quarter gained 28 percent to a record $576.1 million, or $1.15 a share, from $449.3 million, or 90 cents a share.
The per-share figures reflect a three-for-two stock split that became effective May 24, the company said.
Travelers said net income for the first nine months of the year hit a record $1.69 billion, or $3.38 a share, up from $1.23 billion, or $2.45 a share.
Revenues for the period increased 16 percent to $15.6 billion from $13.4 billion.
Travelers said its operating earnings for the nine months jumped 36 percent to $1.62 billion -- nearly equal to operating earnings for all of last year.

The company reported strong results at Travelers/Aetna Property Casualty Corp., in which Travelers has an 82 percent stake. The subsidiary posted net income of $247 million, or 62 cents a share, on revenues of $2.45 billion.

Travelers/Aetna, which provides homeowners and auto insurance to individuals and insurance products to businesses, was created in April, when Travelers acquired Aetna Casualty and Surety and formed a new publicly traded company.

The company said Travelers/Aetna was on target in integrating operations and was ahead of schedule in its plan to achieve $300 million in annual savings. After only six months in operation, nearly half of those targeted savings have already been achieved, Travelers said.
Travelers also said its Smith Barney brokerage unit showed continued strength, with net income increasing 17 percent to $208.7 million from $177.9 million on total revenues of $1.89 billion.
The company said Smith Barney's return on equity grew by almost a third to 32.2 percent -- one of the highest in the securities industry.
Travelers Grooup stock added $1.375 to $53.25 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
